methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a well-defined retrospective cohort from Oncoshare-Lung (Stanford) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria (7,060 -> 312 de novo stage IV EGFR-mutant patients), manual annotation of 592 radiology reports (1,807 lesions) by three trained annotators, and multivariable Cox regression with pre-specified covariates (age, ECOG PS, sex, treatment delay). Methodological limitations include single-center design, reliance on the authors' own derived composite score with the same cohort used for both discovery and evaluation (no external validation), inconsistent radiology size reporting (acknowledged), and inability to abstract PFS retrospectively. Statistical rigor is comparatively strong: Bonferroni correction applied across 18 metrics (alpha = 0.00278), complete-case analysis justified by <2.2% missingness, multiple sensitivity analyses (time zero change, mutation-type stratification, second-line therapy as time-varying covariate), and reporting of 95% confidence intervals. Power calculation is not explicit.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b). Clinical relevance is high in a practical sense: the composite score (number of metastatic organs + bone metastasis) is derived from routinely available clinical data and directly addresses a contemporary treatment dilemma (osimertinib monotherapy vs FLAURA2-style combination intensification) by proposing a way to identify low-burden patients who might safely avoid combination toxicity. Findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before practice change.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to this observational cohort. Reporting is thorough: clear flow diagram (Fig 1), explicit inclusion/exclusion counts, pre-specified confounders, annotation protocol documented in the Data Supplement, sensitivity analyses described, and limitations candidly addressed (size reporting heterogeneity, missing PFS, single-center cohort, need for external validation). Multiple testing correction is explicit. Gaps include limited discussion of selection bias from complete-case analysis and no explicit STROBE checklist reference. Data availability: Oncoshare-Lung access is implicit but no explicit statement, and annotation data/code for composite score calculation are not clearly deposited.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors acknowledge prior work on tumor burden in EGFR-TKI settings (Cha 2015 Clin Lung Cancer, FLAURA2 post-hoc analyses, Delasos 2024) and position theirs as the first real-world comprehensive evaluation incorporating RECIST-unmeasured metastases (notably bone) and a practical composite score in the osimertinib era. The methodologic advance (EHR-based manual annotation including bone and brain) is incremental but meaningful; the finding that bone metastasis and organ count dominate prognosis is consistent with broader meta-analyses (refs 38-40). Not paradigm-shifting; it represents a targeted extension with practical clinical utility.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured in JCO-style format with concise results, well-organized tables/figures, and a balanced discussion. Limitations are explicitly and candidly discussed (size-reporting inconsistencies, PFS unreliability, need for external validation). Statistical reporting is precise with HRs, 95% CIs, and p-values. Some dense methods paragraphs could be streamlined, but overall the presentation is publication-quality.

key_strengths: Well-curated real-world cohort (312 patients) with granular manual lesion annotation (1,807 lesions from 592 reports) across osimertinib era
Pre-specified multivariable Cox modeling with Bonferroni correction for multiple testing across 18 metrics
Multiple sensitivity and subgroup analyses (time zero, mutation type, second-line as time-varying) support robustness
Practical composite score using routinely documented clinical data addressing contemporary monotherapy-vs-combination decision (FLAURA2, MARIPOSA)
Capture of RECIST-unmeasured metastases (notably bone) addresses gap in trial-based analyses
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external validation cohort; composite score derived and evaluated on same population risks optimism
Osimertinib subgroup (n=123) has wide CIs and attenuated significance (P=0.03) for key survival finding
Progression-free survival could not be abstracted, limiting biomarker interpretation
Radiology report heterogeneity in lesion size measurement introduces measurement error
Data and annotation code not explicitly deposited, limiting reproducibility of composite score construction
No formal power calculation or pre-registered analysis plan mentioned
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent hypothesis-generating retrospective real-world analysis with appropriate statistical rigor but limited by single-center scope, no external validation, and unavailable PFS data; best positioned at Tier 3 (e.g., European Journal of Cancer, Cancers, JCO Clinical Cancer Informatics) with minor revisions to address validation and data availability.
